## Triangle inequality · Both bounds {#fv1-triangle-combined .fv-lesson }

$$
\boxed{\bigl||\underset{\sim}{a}|-|\underset{\sim}{b}|\bigr|\leq|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|\leq|\underset{\sim}{a}|+|\underset{\sim}{b}|}
$$

The resultant's magnitude lies between the **difference** and the **sum** of the two lengths.

```{=html}
<div class="fv-bound-summary"><div><h3>Lower bound</h3><p>Opposite directions give the greatest cancellation.</p><p class="small">Equality for non-zero vectors pointing in opposite directions.</p></div><div><h3>Upper bound</h3><p>The straight-line distance cannot exceed the two-part route.</p><p class="small">Equality for non-zero vectors pointing in the same direction.</p></div></div>
<p class="small">If either vector is zero, equality holds in both bounds.</p>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §1.3 · p. 9</div>

::: {.notes}
Connect the two demonstrations. The outer absolute value makes the lower bound non-negative regardless of which vector is longer. With magnitudes 4 and 3, the resultant ranges from 1 to 7. Equal non-zero magnitudes can cancel to zero. Both inequalities hold in two and three dimensions.
:::
